body:
15. A script `r7-place.sh <scratch-root> <viola> [--rehearse]`, in the shape of `scripts/r3-focus.sh` and
    `scripts/r2-open.sh`.
    - Its frame: `set -u`; a `trap` that closes what it opened on every exit path; `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` /
      `VIOLA_BIN` unset first (tests · decision/live-rig-clean-start). Its header states that it opens ONE terminal
      window and starts no claude.
    - **The stand-in**: a 0700 `/bin/sh` file named `claude` in a scratch bin dir put first on PATH. It answers
      `--version` alone with one fixed line, exits 0, and otherwise ignores the wrapper's leading arguments and
      sleeps. The CLI is therefore unverified, so the start writes no trust record and runs no automatic verify.
    - Preconditions, read first, each failure printing `r7: red precondition=<word>` and starting nothing:
      - the scratch root absent;
      - `foot` and `hyprctl` on PATH;
      - `hyprctl locked` reading `false`;
      - the stand-in's `--version` answered;
      - the build's hash printed right before the start (verification-harness 2026-10-20).
    - **The reading**:
      - Read `hyprctl -j monitors` and take the focused monitor's active workspace `A`.
      - Choose a target `N`: the lowest of 1–9 that is not `A` and that `hyprctl -j workspaces` lists with no window,
        else the lowest that is not `A`.
      - Run `<viola> --home <scratch>/home open r7place --workspace N --json -- claude`, its PATH holding the
        stand-in, and read its `placement`.
      - Read the monitors again: `A2`.
      - `active=unchanged` when `A2 == A`, `moved` when not, `unread` when either read failed.
    - **The close**: the opened instance's wrapper ended by TERM (its pid read from `snapshot.json`'s `data.pid`;
      verification-harness 2026-11-19), its foot window waited gone. The script dispatches no focus of its own.
    - Its one verdict line, from a closed set:
      - `r7: green placement=placed active=unchanged` only when both hold;
      - `r7: red placement=<word> active=<unchanged|moved|unread>` otherwise.
    - `--rehearse` runs the same steps over the fake `foot` and `hyprctl` (terminal mode) in a scratch bin dir with the
      same stand-in. It cannot reach the real compositor. Its verdict line comes first, then the last line
      `r7: rehearsed — not a live reading`, so its output is never a record the gated entry may take.

- Eight time bounds viola holds (wait timeout and cap, MCP call deadline, dialog hold, send readiness gate, paste write, confirmation windows, agents read, the start's Claude config lock wait) fall on the driver, viola's child or viola's own start; no key is blocked, refused or delayed by them. The start's verify stop grace, the wait before a stopped start's verify child is killed, likewise falls on viola's own child only: no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it and the wheel is untouched. An MCP frame tool call (send, wait, last, answer) that outlives the MCP call deadline (`viola_mcp::MCP_CALL_DEADLINE`) ends `instance-unreachable` / `call-deadline`, the outcome of a send unknown; only the MCP frame tools write that detail, never the CLI, whose exit-21 cause set stays six. The one `claude agents --json` read `viola list`, `viola revive` and `viola adopt` each make (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) is killed at 5 s, a bound on viola's own child only: a failed, oversize, malformed or timed-out read fails open, and no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it. `viola wait` returns `{timed_out:true}` only for a timeout the caller passes in. The MCP `wait` tool (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) clamps its `timeout_ms` to `WAIT_CAP`, also its default when the caller passes none (`viola_mcp::wait_timeout`), so an MCP `wait` with no timeout is answered `timed-out` at `WAIT_CAP`: a bound on the driver only (the hidden, plugin-run `viola mcp` serves a driving Claude session, never a person), no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it, and the wheel is untouched. A raised dialog takes a `viola answer` only within the dialog hold (`config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, PROVISIONAL bounds; chunk 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver); at the hold's end the wrapper replies `null` and appends one `dialog-expired` line, the dialog renders for the human in the `claude` TUI, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` / `unknown-dialog` (exit 13) — the hold bounds the driver, never the human: any human key still hands the held dialog back at once, whatever the hold. A `viola send` on a verified CLI waits in the readiness gate for at most `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (8.5 s) and is then refused `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` with nothing typed; a key pressed during the wait goes to the child and takes the wheel at once, and the waiting send is then refused `human-typing`. Once typed, a confirmed `viola send` waits for its confirmation within `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` (10 s), and a `/compact` send on a verified CLI within its own `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s, PROVISIONAL, architecture [Delivery Confirmation]); a send not confirmed inside its window is `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`: a bound on the driver only, the confirm wait takes no key and blocks, refuses or delays none, and the wheel is untouched. A start's window step waits at most 5 s for its own terminal's window to appear in the compositor's client list, each compositor read through the Hyprland seam is bounded at 5 s a reply (the window step, viola open, viola focus), and viola open waits at most 30 s for the instance it started to come live, then reads not-live; each falls on viola's own start or verb, never on a key typed into a session, and never moves the wheel.
